new_value: Implemented ManhattanGrid in python/src/lichen/sim/mobility.py:673, extending the module's actual ABC MobilityPattern (no BaseMobility exists here). Grid coordinate system: square grid anchored at (min_x, min_y) with configurable spacing_m (:700), grid points at min + k*spacing for indices fitting inside area_bounds (_grid_size/_axis_value). Public snap_to_grid(x, y)/:729 maps any position to the nearest on-grid point clamped into bounds (via _snap_axis_index). Initial placement: on first step() the node is snapped onto the nearest grid point (dt_us=0 gives placement-only). Movement is linear along grid lines only: _pick_next_cell()/:806 chooses a random adjacent grid cell and the node travels straight toward it at speed_m_s, re-choosing at each intersection; state is tracked as integer grid indices to avoid float round-trip drift; degenerate single-point grids are a safe no-op. Pause probability at intersections is parent-bead 2.11 scope, intentionally not included here. Tests in python/tests/sim/test_manhattan_grid.py (17 tests): snap correctness incl. clamping and partial last cell, spacing/speed/bounds validation, on-grid initial placement, axis-locked movement, speed along a leg, intersection visits, in-bounds over 200 fast steps, z propagation, degenerate grid, reset, determinism, manager attach. Targeted suite 78 passed; full tests/sim/ 1610 passed, 36 skipped; ruff clean; mypy strict clean.
